Second round of the same film: improve the locked cut-v5d of "The Little Match Girl" (2-minute English short film, 115–125 seconds) into a new locked cut.

What the first round left: several shots are still images with a slow push-in instead of motion, including the ending; the video model hit its daily request cap, and its safety filter refused the ending shots of the girl at dawn and the townspeople finding her. A slow push-in rendered on whole pixels judders (one-pixel steps every few frames), as at about 0:48–0:51 and 1:50 of cut-v5d.

This round there is a second video model (video-generation-wan) beside the first, whose daily cap resets at 07:00 UTC. Replace the remaining still shots with moving shots where it serves the film, find a way to tell the ending that the video models will make, and make any push-in that remains move smoothly. Keep what already works: the story, the style, the narration, the music and the length.

Deliver one playable `film.mp4` (H.264 video, AAC audio, 1080p or 720p) with English subtitles, burned in or as a sidecar `.srt`.

A synthetic check of one resource before a real film. It is not a film: do only this, briefly, and do not retry a failed step another way.

editor, in its first turn: read `ht-resource describe video-generation-wan`; make a 640x360 PNG first frame with `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc=size=640x360 -frames:v 1 f.png`; submit exactly one wan2.7-i2v task of 3 seconds at 720P as the description says; poll it until it ends; download the video and check it with ffprobe. Write `probe.md` in your repository with each step's HTTP status, the task status, the ffprobe line, or the exact error (at most 10 lines), and push it.

director approves the release if editor's probe.md shows a downloaded video; otherwise it says which step failed.

Make a 2-minute (115–125 seconds) English-language short film of Hans Christian Andersen's "The Little Match Girl" (1845); the public-domain English text is in the inputs.

Tell the whole story — the freezing New Year's Eve street, the five matches and their visions (the stove, the roast goose, the Christmas tree, her grandmother), and the morning after — so that a first-time viewer follows it and is moved. The visual style is the director's choice.

Sound: spoken English narration as the main voice, with a few lines of dialogue where they help, plus music and sound effects. Add English subtitles, burned in or as a sidecar `.srt` file. Characters, places and the visual style must stay consistent from shot to shot.

Deliver one playable `film.mp4` (H.264 video, AAC audio, 1080p or 720p) that a web browser plays.

A synthetic check of one resource before a real film. It is not a film: do only this, briefly, and do not retry a failed step another way.

editor and director, each in its first turn: read `ht-resource describe image-generation`, make exactly one request as it says for a small image of a lit match in snow, save the image, check it with `file`, and write `probe.md` in your repository with the HTTP status and the file's type, or the exact error (at most 10 lines). The director then approves the release if both images were made; otherwise it says which failed.

A synthetic check of this world's resources before a real film. It is not a film: do only this, briefly, and do not retry a failed step another way.

editor, in its first turn: for each of video-generation, image-generation, speech, music, sound-effects and film-understanding, read `ht-resource describe <id>` and make exactly one request as it says — a 3-second video of a lit match in falling snow; a small image of a match; the spoken sentence "It was terribly cold."; a 10-second piano cue; a 1-second match-strike effect; and a question to film-understanding about the 3-second video you made. Save each result, check each media file with ffprobe, and write `probe.md` in your repository: per resource, the HTTP status, the media type, duration or size from ffprobe, or the exact error (at most 10 lines). Push it and publish the video as a release `probe-1`.

director, in its first turn: make a 2-second test video with `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc=duration=2:size=320x240:rate=24 -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:duration=2 -shortest -c:v libx264 -c:a aac t.mp4`, ask film-understanding (gemini-3.8-flash) what it sees and hears, ask audio-understanding what it hears in the same file's audio, and write `probe.md` in your repository with each HTTP status and answer or exact error. Then, when editor's `probe.md` is pushed, read it, and approve the release if every editor step and both of yours returned media or an answer; otherwise say which failed.

Make "Paper Boat", a 60-second test film.

- Picture: one key frame made with the world's image generation: a red paper boat on a calm lake at dawn, in a wide shot. The film is a slow push-in on that frame for its whole length, with the title "Paper Boat" over the first 5 seconds.
- Sound: a soft 220 Hz tone for the whole film, fading in over the first 2 seconds and out over the last 2.
- Master: `film/paper-boat.mp4`, 1920x1080 at 25 fps, H.264 at a constant 24 Mbit/s (about 180 MB), AAC stereo at 48 kHz, exactly 60 seconds long.
- The locked film is the master in the film root, also published as a release file so that it can be watched in a web browser.
